You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Go in production
G2: Python services (Django/FastAPI)
G3: gRPC
G4: Terraform authoring
G5: team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming production Go or Python service experience to match a Python/Go ad
T2: Listing FastAPI/Django/gRPC because the ad asks for them
T3: Turning the Go side project into professional experience
T4: Calling him team lead because he runs a guild

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Software Engineer
Lisbon, Portugal | daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | +351 555 010 202 |
linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example

Backend engineer with 7 years of experience building and operating production services in Java and
Kotlin, including Spring Boot microservices, REST APIs, PostgreSQL-backed systems and Kafka event
workflows. Experienced in query performance improvements, automated testing, CI/CD, Docker and
AWS deployments. Interested in moving into a Python-focused backend role; Python experience to date
is limited to scripts and small Jenkins helpers.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Backend: Java (8–17), Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, Kotlin (basic), Python
(scripting), Go (learning)
APIs and messaging: REST, OpenAPI, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Databases and performance: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis, JPA query tuning
Cloud and delivery: Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Jenkins, Git, Linux
Testing: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Spring Cloud Contract
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | Lisbon | Jan 2022–Present
• Develop and maintain 7 Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices supporting policy quoting and claims
intake.
• Designed and versioned an OpenAPI 3 REST API for partner quoting; onboarded 12 broker
partners, handling around 400,000 quote requests per month.
• Added per-partner rate limiting and contract tests with Spring Cloud Contract for the quoting API.
• Implemented Kafka idempotent consumers and a transactional outbox for the claims workflow,
reducing duplicate claim records from approximately 40 per week to zero over the following quarter.
• Improved quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds by adding Redis caching
and resolving JPA N+1 queries.
• Deploy services to Kubernetes on AWS EKS using Helm charts and Jenkins pipelines; use AWS S3
and SQS in service work.
• Participate in a one-week-per-month on-call rotation; handled a significant Kafka lag incident in

• Run the backend guild meeting every two weeks (since 2024).
• Built a small internal Kotlin / Spring Boot service to render policy PDFs from templates and wrote
the team’s Kotlin coding guidelines.

• Extracted email and SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a separate Spring Boot
service using RabbitMQ and Thymeleaf.
Junior Developer (Internship, then Full-time) | CodeFarol Lda | Porto | Jul 2018–Aug 2019

LANGUAGES
English (fluent; professional working language at Tejo Insurance Tech)
Portuguese (fluent)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Tessel Cargo Software hiring team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) position on the Routing & Tracking team. I
bring seven years of professional experience building and operating backend services in Java
and Spring Boot, seven years of backend experience in Java and Spring Boot, a
comparable-language foundation for a role working mainly in Python. I am keen to apply that
production experience while developing further in Python; my Python experience to date has
been limited to scripts and small Jenkins helpers.
In my current role at Tejo Insurance Tech, I develop and maintain seven services supporting
policy quoting and claims intake. I designed a versioned REST API used by 12 broker
partners for around 400,000 quote requests per month, and improved its p99 latency from 1.8
seconds to 450 milliseconds by adding Redis caching and resolving JPA N+1 queries in a
PostgreSQL-backed service. I have also worked with Kafka event workflows, implementing
idempotent consumers and a transactional outbox that reduced duplicate claim records from
around 40 per week to zero over the following quarter. These experiences have given me a
practical focus on dependable APIs, data correctness and performance.
I also bring hands-on experience with automated testing, CI/CD and operating services: at
Viajar Online, I raised payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers;
at Tejo, I contribute to CI/CD delivery by deploying services with Docker and Helm to
Kubernetes on AWS EKS through Jenkins pipelines. I take part in a monthly on-call rotation
and handled a significant Kafka lag incident, contributing an incident write-up that was well
regarded. I would welcome the opportunity to bring this production experience to Tessel’s
shipment tracking platform while developing further in Python.
Tessel’s focus on end-to-end ownership, clear communication and operational reliability
resonates with how I approach backend work. I would be glad to discuss how my experience
designing REST/OpenAPI APIs, building Kafka event-driven services, tuning PostgreSQL
queries, and operating production services could contribute to the Routing & Tracking team.
Thank you for considering my application.
Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
